budgets.rule: No longer than the longest bullet already in the file it joins. The generated AGENTS.md is 5017 bytes over twelve bullets; a thirteenth that is not the longest one there cannot be the reason the file stopped being read.

One 80x24 terminal screen, which is the unscrollable unit a person actually sees. The only artifact of the four with no live product comparandum: `s0ma --help` would be the obvious one, but argparse renders it at the running terminal's width, so it is not a fixed number (40 columns gives 5256 bytes, 200 gives 3436). A navigation stub that must be byte-deterministic has to be authored at a fixed width rather than formatted by argparse.

One line, no longer than the shorter of the two conditional lines already riding this channel (the feedback-offer line at 319 bytes, the narration line at 413). The longest line on the channel is also the only one measured under-complying — the narration line lands at 44% — so a documentation pointer may not become the new longest thing here.
At most a fifth of the served instructions blob. Every session pays for this text once, whatever it does next, so no single concern may claim more than a fifth of it.
